title: Dissolution - the world and everything in it does not exist outside of your observation
author: Rick_grin
selftext:
Dissolution \[demo\] is a hardcore survival game where reality dissolves beyond your observation. It's not fog of war, the world and everything in it literally doesn't exist unless something is watching it.

It is almost entirely built by Claude Opus 4.5/6, with sprites created through my own skill with GPT Image 1.5 and Nano Banana.

Half the sprites I had to polish manually, but otherwise the AI did an amazing job.

Sounds were all selected manually.

You can play it fully free: [https://riccardogrin.itch.io/dissolution](https://riccardogrin.itch.io/dissolution)

Really happy with where it is as a demo, though there are definitely gaps that AI can't quite help with (yet):

* sprite animations
* lacking some hit/enemy/mob/ambient sounds
* more progression
* use for every single game item
* some UI is still just temp and boring
* the final two bosses need some more work to make them a fun fight

Feedback welcome, keen to hear all of it, the good and bad!!

comments.author: Revelation12Studios
comments.body:
That’s a really interesting concept. 

Regarding sprite sheets, there are work arounds: what I do is get an image, generate a video with it and plop it into my video-to-sprite sheet app I vibe coded. Works really well.

replies.author: Rick_grin
replies.body:
Thats an interesting idea.  
Ill have to look into it.

I was actually about to create a sprite animation skill for Claude, but i wasn't thinking of going the video route.

comments.author: mana_hoarder
comments.body: Curious, how does the premise that things don't exist unless they are inside the view actually affect the gameplay?

replies.author: Rick_grin
replies.body:
I think i've only scratched the surface of what the concept can really do, but yes, it makes a difference to game play, but even more can be done.

So, given that outside of observations objects/animals/enemies/... dont exist, if you see an enemy you can just run away, but on the other hand, if you place a workbench down and walk away, the workbench disappears forever.

Those are just basic examples of how it can affect gameplay. I think thematically this can be push further to create a really hardcore survival experience. Sticking to the theme/idea and building up a world around how it all got devoured by the void and what you can do about it, or potentially become part of the void, I think has something really interesting to it.

replies.author: mana_hoarder
replies.body: I dunno, man. Back in the NES era, every game had this feature. Having a game with memory was revolutionary. But maybe you can somehow make this work thematically. I wish you luck.

replies.author: checkwithanthony
replies.body: Do they spawn as you see them or are they there just dormant? As in if I run away.. does it despawn? Can I run back into it etc?

replies.author: Rick_grin
replies.body:
The world, animals, enemies, and all the rocks/trees/bushes, generate as you walk and get entirely deleted from where you walk away.
So if you walk back, something new gets generated.

replies.author: checkwithanthony
replies.body: The world? Even the map? If you walk up to water then walk back then back again might the actual map be different and now theres a building there?

replies.author: Rick_grin
replies.body:
To an extent, yes. If you walk away and back from an area, a stucture may appear that was never there before.

The terrain tiles will also change.

However, for the current setup I have made it so that biomes, rivers, and oceans remain in the same place.

So if for example you walk back and forth in the forest you keep seeing the terrain tiles change, and a structure may even appear, but the forest biome will remain the same biome.

This could be changed, but it is a fair bit more complex to do it smoothly so that you dont create a messy patchwork of biomes.

replies.author: checkwithanthony
replies.body: I think I like your way much better.

replies.author: Own-Letterhead-3432
replies.body:
Hey there. Nice project you have there. 

I thought it might work well for the gameplay, if stuff doesn’t disappear immediately but rather mutate / morph with other stuff from the games item list over time. So returning to an object would make it more interesting. - a bit like the movie „Assimilation“ where biomass gets randomly recombined, resulting sometimes in very dangerous entities. But you could take it a step further by adding structures into the list of recombination too. Resulting in houses, portals, castles etc. being morphed into living creatures with different needs. So the player needs to hurry up to complete a task before the structure walks away or gets morphed into a tree like being loosing its original functionality. I think that way the player would engage more with the environment and just running away won’t be first choice anymore. 

Just a thought.   
Good luck

comments.author: DocHolidayPhD
comments.body: ... is your main character blind as a bat and can only see 5 feet in any direction around them? Why can they see behind them while also seeing ahead of them at the same time?

replies.author: Rick_grin
replies.body: Im thinking to add a sort of whisp character or something that the player holds which makes the observation aura around them. So it's less like "what the player is seeing" and more like "what the whisp/lantern allows them to see". It's meant to feel more like the world has been devoured by the void and less like you are just using your eyes to look around you.

replies.author: Rick_grin
replies.body:
Yes you can actually play it.
There are 3 bosses, tool/weapon progression, farming, bunch of different biomes, …
